description: Write the comprehensive review article (main.tex and references.bib) on Deep Learning for Earthquake Early Warning Systems: Single-Station vs Multi-Station Approaches. This is a 30+ page article written from the perspective of an expert professor in AI and seismology, targeting Earth-Science Reviews (Elsevier). The article must be research-intensive with 150+ real references.
steps: Create /projects/sandbox/sonet-product/artikel_review_2/references.bib with 150+ real, verifiable bibliographic entries covering: seminal EEW papers (Allen 2003, Nakamura 1988, Wu 2005), deep learning foundations (LeCun 2015, Krizhevsky 2012, He 2016, Vaswani 2017, Hochreiter 1997), single-station DL methods (PhaseNet - Zhu & Beroza 2019, EQTransformer - Mousavi 2020, CREIME - Bilal 2022, TEAM - Munchmeyer 2021, DeepQuake - Perol 2018, GPD - Ross 2018, ConvNetQuake - Perol 2018, PICK-net, PhasePApy), multi-station DL methods (ELARMS, EPIC, FinDer, GENIE - McBrearty 2023, LPPN - van den Ende 2020, MagNet, NEIC methods, GNN-based associators - Munchmeyer 2021, Zhang 2021), benchmark datasets (STEAD - Mousavi 2019, INSTANCE - Michelini 2021, LEN-DB, DiTing - Zhao 2023, SCEDC, NCEDC), transformer-based (Seismogram Transformer, EQGraphNet), operational EEW systems (JMA, ShakeAlert, SASMEX, CWA Taiwan, PRESTo Italy), and review/survey papers (Bergen 2019, Kong 2019, Mousavi 2022). All entries must have correct authors, titles, journals/conferences, years, volumes, pages where applicable.

Create /projects/sandbox/sonet-product/artikel_review_2/main.tex with the following comprehensive structure using elsarticle [review,authoryear] document class, targeting 30+ pages. Follow the exact formatting pattern from artikel_review/main.tex (same packages, same style). The article structure must include: (1) Title: 'Deep Learning for Earthquake Early Warning Systems: A Comprehensive Review of Single-Station versus Multi-Station Approaches' (2) Authors: Ahmad R. Purnama as corresponding author with affiliations at Dept Computer Science and Dept Earth Sciences, Universitas Diponegoro (3) Abstract: ~300 words covering motivation, scope, key findings, conclusions (4) Keywords: Deep Learning, Earthquake Early Warning, Single-Station, Multi-Station, Seismology, CNN, RNN, Transformer, Real-time (5) Section 1 Introduction (~3 pages): EEW motivation, traditional vs DL approaches, single vs multi station paradigm, scope and contributions (6) Section 2 Fundamentals of EEW Systems (~3 pages): Physical principles, operational systems worldwide table, processing pipeline, on-site vs regional approaches (7) Section 3 Deep Learning Foundations for Seismology (~4 pages): CNN architectures, RNN/LSTM, Attention/Transformer, autoencoders, transfer learning, data augmentation (8) Section 4 Single-Station Deep Learning Methods (~5 pages): P/S wave detection and picking (PhaseNet, GPD, EQTransformer), single-station magnitude estimation, single-station location approximation, back-azimuth estimation, advantages and limitations (9) Section 5 Multi-Station Deep Learning Methods (~5 pages): Network-based detection and association, multi-station source characterization, GNN-based approaches, ensemble methods, ground motion prediction, advantages and limitations (10) Section 6 Comparative Analysis: Single vs Multi-Station (~4 pages): Performance comparison table with metrics (precision, recall, F1, MAE, latency), use case scenarios, cost-benefit analysis, hybrid approaches (11) Section 7 Benchmark Datasets and Evaluation (~3 pages): STEAD, INSTANCE, LEN-DB, DiTing, regional catalogs, evaluation metrics, SeisBench framework (12) Section 8 Deployment and Real-time Challenges (~2 pages): Latency requirements, edge computing, model compression, fault tolerance (13) Section 9 Future Directions and Open Problems (~3 pages): Foundation models, physics-informed neural networks, federated learning, uncertainty quantification, explainability, multi-hazard integration (14) Section 10 Conclusions (~1 page). Include at least 3 comprehensive comparison tables, 2+ TikZ figures (architecture diagrams), mathematical formulations where appropriate, and use \citep/\citet throughout for all claims.
Ensure the document compiles without errors: run pdflatex + bibtex + pdflatex + pdflatex compilation chain
Verify the compiled PDF is at least 30 pages
acceptance_criteria: File artikel_review_2/main.tex exists and is a valid LaTeX document
File artikel_review_2/references.bib exists with 150+ bibliography entries
Document compiles without fatal errors using pdflatex + bibtex
Generated PDF (artikel_review_2/main.pdf) is at least 30 pages
All sections listed above are present and substantive (not placeholder text)
Citations use real published papers with correct metadata
Document follows elsarticle format consistent with Earth-Science Reviews
Article is written at expert academic level appropriate for a high-impact review journal
verification: Run: cd /projects/sandbox/sonet-product/artikel_review_2 && pdflatex -interaction=nonstopmode main.tex && bibtex main && pdflatex -interaction=nonstopmode main.tex && pdflatex -interaction=nonstopmode main.tex
Run: pdfinfo main.pdf | grep Pages (should show >= 30)
Run: grep '\\section' main.tex | wc -l (should show >= 10 sections)
